_doc: Aspen Motorsports Park through Lake Murray v4's engine (ledger 0078). The line, widths and profile are tracks/aspen's (installed 0.67.1), read by tools/lm_engine_intake.py; the profile is the measured one with the elevation stage's grade cap undone; no lidar camber (the G10 survey found no usable cloud here: source/lidar/camber-survey/README.md), so flat; the 3DEP grid is this port's own fetch (the live track commits none); the edge is the circuit's (no curb, no sidewalk). Every other key is the live track's, copied; the live config is untouched.

source._smooth_window_doc: 2026-11-01 (ledger 0060, High Plains' lesson): source/osm_fixes.json is a list of 64 OSM nodes (8 m apart on the corners, up to 302 m on the straights), not a 1 Hz GPS drive; from_track's 5-fix moving average put the line 3.33 m median / 6.30 p95 / 7.36 m max off the source polygon (corners cut by most of the 9 m road) and shortened the lap 1,676 -> 1,600 m. 0 = no smoothing: the line is the OSM polygon resampled at 3 m (build_mesh still corner-rounds it for the sweep).
source._note: Real Aspen Motorsports Park (550 Raceway Rd, Woody Creek, CO). From OSM highway=raceway way 192313782 (1-mile road course), native CCW winding reversed to CW, resampled to 3 m via scripts.gps.from_track. Elevation from USGS 3DEP bare-earth (mountain site, do NOT flatten); NO banking (road course).

road_profile._doc: Flat road course — no banking. dips/cambers intentionally empty; deck follows bare-earth 3DEP.
road_profile._fold_pads_doc: 2026-11-03 (ledger 0074): the engine reads the 160 deg final hairpin (apex at lap 1,573 m) as a fold and, its +-60 m chord grade reading 0.9 %, laid a paved disc and a w/2+16 = 20.5 m flat zone that snapped every pavement vertex to the apex height. The corner itself climbs ~2.4 % (3DEP), so the zone rims were steps: +0.23 m at the entry and -0.20 m at the exit inside one 3 m segment, all 17 severe steps at 1,551-1,557 and 1,597-1,599 m. The ribbon sweeps this corner without folding (R 12.6 m at 9 m wide), so no pad: the engine's +-40 m fold plateau stays.

route._orientation_doc: Research 2026-07-20: Aspen Motorsports Park runs CLOCKWISE (official map corners 1-7 CW; crash-report geometry corroborates). Our ring is already CW. S/F on the short N-S chute south of the final hairpin (~39.2669,-106.8800), cars heading SSW; checkered timing stand beside it. Pit lane: east side of the S/F chute (driver's left), ~100-150 m, splits at hairpin exit, rejoins after S/F.

edge._grass_clearance_doc: 0.1.4 (PC, 2026-11-09; Kevin, asked whether the other circuit tracks have Milford's fast-curve edge mess: "Yes, check them"; Milford 0.1.6 is the same fix, ledger 0087): the strip's outer lip 2 cm under the lane edge (profile point 3 at -grass_clearance = +0.08 over the unlifted edge; the lane edge at +0.10). engine-july's prep holds the ground past the ROAD edge at the lane edge's height - 0.02 for 3 m (its contact band), so the lower lip lay in a gutter with a wall of ground at its lip. Measured on the installed 0.1.3 (gate OBJ, every 10 m, both sides; strip_gutter.py): the strip's lip 14 cm under the lane edge; the ground just past it stood more than 5 cm over the lip at 16 of 280 side-stations, more than 10 cm at 5 (max 12 cm). Flush with the band, nothing stands over it
edge._doc: the circuit edge (ledger 0078): no curb, no sidewalk. The asphalt edge is held at road height for 0.30 m and the run-off ground meets it 0.15 m lower over 1.0 m [invented: the flush meet the drive gate reads as no drop]; the ground beyond is the assembler's conform to the road, then the 3DEP surface: the real run-off level.

route._kerbs_doc: Aspen's three red / white kerbs (tracks/aspen/source/edges/kerbs.json: NAIP 2023 0.3 m, ends by eye on end zooms, offsets by their blocks: ledger 0081 round 3); built at their measured place by tools/author_kerbs_blend.py

road_wear._doc: ledger 0084 (Kevin 2026-11-07: "road textures to include wear along where tires run, in a realistic manner" / "For tracks we'll use racing lines" / "Which will help darken curbs realistically"; 2026-11-10, to the Mac: "build the road wear for the other circuits on the pc overnight"). High Plains 0.1.7's bake (tools/road_wear_blend.py, last in prep): the large-scale tone off the aerial, registered to the built road, under the stock cracked asphalt kept as the 4 m detail (ksPerPixelMultiMap_NMDetail); the rubber is the photo's own (rubber 'photo': no drawn band); the traced race kerbs get the line's darkening where it rides them (kerbs). scripts/aerial/road_wear.py DEFAULTS has every number, marked measured / model / invented.
road_wear._surfaces_doc: the road and the edge strip beside it (ledger 0087's 1KERB_sidewalk), as Milford and High Plains: the strip shares the atlas so the rubber where the line clips the edge carries on over it
road_wear._texel_doc: as High Plains 0.1.7: 0.25 m keeps the detail multiplier whole (4096 px x 0.25 / 4 = 256; the bake refuses a fractional one) and is finer than a 0.3 m photo's pixel
road_wear._rubber_doc: Kevin 2026-11-10: "Use the photo's rubber" (ledger 0084), the default for the 0.3 m circuits: the asphalt gets no drawn band, the photo's tone carries the rubber; the bake measures the photo's darkening across the line against its mirror (scripts/aerial/road_wear.photo_rubber), and the gate's photo_rubber row needs the photo's own depth >= 0.03
